extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Senators, policy makers, USPTO officials, patent practitioners, and industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the legislative and policy criteria in the Congressional debate and supporting letters about S.23 (the America Invents Act of 2011), i.e., standards and reforms proposed to improve U.S. patent law, USPTO operations, patent quality, and litigation certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve and harmonize USPTO operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve and harmonize operations at the Patent and Trademark Office; provide the PTO with the resources it needs to work through its backlog and improve service to applicants and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bill provisions include fee-setting authority, operational flexibility (including contracting for searches), establishment of satellite offices, Three-Track (prioritized) examination, and other administrative reforms aimed at reducing pendency (backlog currently exceeds ~700,000) and increasing speed and efficiency without taxpayer funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the quality of patents that are issued so that issued patents are more likely to be valid, thereby benefiting both patent owners and users and reducing the harm from dubious patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms to achieve higher quality include earlier third-party submission of prior art, supplemental examination, post-grant opposition/review procedures, improved inter partes review processes, and more examiner-accessible prior art to help examiners make correct patentability decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide more certainty in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide more certainty and predictability in patent litigation to curb abusive litigation practices and reduce unpredictability that harms innovation and investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions described include court gatekeeping on damages and jury instructions, venue reforms to curb forum shopping, administrative alternatives to costly litigation (post-grant reviews and inter partes reviews), and estoppel provisions that limit re-litigation of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-inventor-to-file system
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition the United States to a first-inventor-to-file system, awarding the patent to the first of two competing inventors to file with the PTO instead of the prior first-to-invent construct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages listed: eliminates costly interference proceedings, creates legal certainty, encourages prompt filing (early disclosure), harmonizes with other patent offices globally, facilitates post-grant oppositions by reducing issues in those proceedings, and builds on prior reforms like provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions of prior art while applications pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow submission of patents or other publications by third parties while applications are still under consideration by the USPTO to increase the prior art made available to examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions should further add to prior art available to examiners and have the potential to greatly enhance patent quality by increasing the adequacy of prior art presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination process
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide patent holders the ability to request a supplemental examination of patents where pertinent history or information may have been omitted in original requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision allows patent holders to improve the quality and defensibility of their patents by surfacing omitted information; the Senate materials state it will strengthen laws to prevent unlawful infringement and improve patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant opposition / 'first window' review (9 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a 'first window' post-grant opposition proceeding open for 9 months after grant to enable early administrative challenges to newly issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to allow the USPTO to weed out patents that should not have been issued, enable early challenges while protecting patent owner rights, and reduce downstream litigation; the approach was recommended by the National Academy of Sciences (2004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial inter partes review with higher threshold and procedural safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the existing inter partes administrative process by establishing an adversarial inter partes review with a higher threshold for initiating proceedings and procedural safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to prevent challengers from harassing patent owners through serial or frivolous filings; intended to provide a faster, less costly administrative alternative to civil litigation while ensuring fairness to patent owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened estoppel standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen estoppel so petitioners cannot raise in later proceedings the same patent issues that were raised or reasonably could have been raised previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces the ability to use post-grant procedures for abusive serial challenges and increases finality of administrative results, thereby lowering costs and uncertainty for patent owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court gatekeeping on damages and jury instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute a gatekeeping role for courts to assess the legal basis for damages awards and jury instructions to constrain excessive or speculative damage awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide more certainty, uniformity, and fairness in damages calculation by tying awards to reliable metrics (e.g., licensing reality) and reducing 'runaway' damage awards that are untethered to licensing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting authority for the USPTO Director (fee-funded operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize the USPTO Director to set or adjust by rule any fee established, authorized, or charged under title 35 and the Trademark Act, with aggregate patent/trademark fee amounts set to recover the Office's estimated processing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants the USPTO flexibility to adjust fees to reflect costs, demand, and workload so operations can be fully cost-recovered from fees (not taxpayer funds), improving productivity and allowing the Office to reduce backlogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated fee reductions for small and micro entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandate a reduction of fees by 50 percent for small entities and 75 percent for micro-entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the bill's provisions to ensure fairness and affordability for smaller applicants while enabling fee-setting authority to overall recover costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curtail patents on tax strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent patents on tax strategies that would encumber taxpayers' and advisers' ability to use the tax law freely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision drafted with PTO input to exclude software tools or systems used to prepare tax returns or manage finances; rationale is to protect voluntary tax compliance and avoid unfair advantages or windfalls from tax-strategy patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational flexibility to contract private entities for searches (PCT and national searches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the USPTO to contract with private companies to perform searches, including as part of PCT searches or potential national searches, to reduce pendency and achieve cost-effective, high-quality searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coalition and supporters argue USPTO management should be empowered to use the best source(s) for searches; PCT operational flexibility has proven to drastically reduce pendency rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform inequitable conduct defense to encourage full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform the inequitable conduct defense to remove incentives that currently discourage full disclosure of all relevant prior art to examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coalition members urge Congress to reform inequitable conduct liability because fear of that defense constrains applicants from fully disclosing prior art, which in turn harms patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curb abusive litigation and forum shopping (venue reforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include provisions on venue to curb forum shopping and reduce abusive litigation practices that create unpredictability and favor certain plaintiffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venue reforms are intended to provide more certainty for defendants and investors and to reduce abusive tactics that lead to unfair settlements or inflated damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance transparency and third-party participation in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase transparency of PTO processes and enable greater third-party participation in the patent review process to assist examiners and strengthen patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include earlier third-party submissions of prior art and allowing explanations to the Office; increased participation improves the adequacy of prior art presented to examiners and therefore patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Track (prioritized) examination and related fee provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for prioritized examination (Three-Track Examination) and consider fee adjustments (including proposals to reduce prioritized-exam fees for small entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritized examination is intended to shorten pendency for applicants who pay for expedited processing; amendments (e.g., Bennet amendment No.116) propose reduced fees for small entities requesting prioritized examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish USPTO satellite offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish additional USPTO satellite offices to improve service, outreach, and processing capacity across regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed (e.g., Bennet amendment No.117) to enhance USPTO service to applicants and the public and to help address backlog and local access to PTO resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage early filing and early public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage both large and small applicants to file more quickly to establish early filing dates and early disclosure of technology to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early filings reduce costly interferences, enable others to build on and improve technology, and align incentives for applicants who plan to file internationally to file promptly in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change to best mode disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the statutory 'best mode' disclosure requirement as part of the reform package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The debate notes changes to the best mode requirement are included in the bill; specific drafting details are not fully enumerated in this excerpt but are cited as a component of the reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on false marking claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Include restrictions on false marking claims to prevent abusive litigation based on false product markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a series of measures intended to reduce frivolous suits and litigation abuses that burden legitimate businesses and the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for government laboratories to commercialize inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase incentives for government laboratories to commercialize inventions and transfer technology to the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to spur commercialization, economic development, and job creation by encouraging government labs to bring inventions to market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove residency restriction for Federal Circuit judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove existing restrictions on the residency of Federal Circuit judges as part of the bill's amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among several diverse provisions in the bill; not primarily a patent quality measure but included in the package of reforms to the patent system and related judiciary matters.
